subject: [PATCH 0/2] mm/gup: batch PTE-mapped large folios in follow_page_mask()

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David (Arm) noted that the current follow_page_mask() interface is about to change, as a new gup-fast path is being introduced, and suggested modifying it to return the number of pinned pages instead of a page mask. He also proposed renaming the function to gup_slow() to make it more similar to the existing gup_fast() interface.

Reviewer David requested that all instances of indentation be converted to two-tab indent on the second and subsequent lines.
reviews.raw_body:
This patch moves us closer towards the GUP-fast path, however, that is about to
change:

	https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260219050250.266876166@ruivo.org/

With that in mind, I guess in the future we want to have:

static long follow_page_mask(struct vm_area_struct *vma,
		unsigned long address, unsigned long end,
		unsigned int flags, struct page **pages)

or even better, now that follow_page() no longer exists, in light of gup_fast():


static long gup_slow(struct vm_area_struct *vma,
		unsigned long address, unsigned long end,
		unsigned int flags, struct page **pages)

Returning the number of pinned pages.


In particular, such an interface would allows us to process multiple
ptes/pmds/... in one go, without having to restart the page table walk all the
time for each non-batchable folio.

And make gup_slow make look more like gup_fast.

I think that's one of the suboptimal things that we inherited from the legacy
follow_page() interface I ripped out a while ago.

... and get rid of that nasty "if (page_increm > 1) {" handling outside of
follow_page_mask().


I'm ok with doing this patch here first, because what I describe is a much
bigger rework.

But being able to pin many pages in one page table walk sounds like another
excellent optimization opportunity, which would even reduce the batching benefit
you see today with patch #2 by simply making PTE processing easier.


I think I can find someone to work on this.

---

While at it, please convert this end the other instances to two-tab indent on
the second+ line.

[...]

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David requested that comments be dropped and instead made directly in the function, specifically mentioning that gup_must_unshare() logic should be above its relevant code.

Reviewer David pointed out that the 'page' argument in follow_page_mask() is not used, suggesting it could be utilized to improve functionality and referencing a similar helper function page_anon_exclusive_batch() in mm/mprotect.c.

Reviewer noted that folio_pte_batch_flags() is only necessary for anonymous folios and suggested an optimization to return early if the folio is not anonymous or if the PTE is writable, instead calling page_anon_exclusive_batch().
reviews.raw_body:
Drop all of these comments and rather comment in the function on the important
bits. For example, the gup_must_unshare() logic belongs above the relevant code
below. If we cannot easily sort it out.

---

Why pass the "page" when it is not even used?

Maybe it should be used? :)

In mm/mprotect.c we do have a page_anon_exclusive_batch() helper already that
would do the right thing. See below.

---

This is really only required for anonymous folios, though.

So likely you could instead just do after the folio_pte_batch_flags() a

nr = folio_pte_batch_flags() ...
if (nr == 1 || !folio_test_anon(folio) || pte_write(pte))
	return nr;
/* Careful with gup_must_unshare(). */
return page_anon_exclusive_batch(0, nr, page, PageAnonExclusive(page));
	

I'll note that the page_anon_exclusive_batch() helper is rather ugly, maybe
you'd just want a nicer one local to this function. It's pretty small in the
end, so you might also just open code a simple loop over PageAnonExclusive().

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author agrees the patch is an optimization and cleanup, indicating a positive sentiment towards the feedback.
reviews.raw_body:
Let me give that a try. This looks like a very
nice optimization, and cleanup.

--

2026-07-29.patch_summary: This patch improves the performance of large folio mapping by batching PTE-mapped large folios in follow_page_mask(). The current implementation walks one page at a time, even for contiguous mappings, which is inefficient. The patch introduces a new interface that returns the number of pages instead of a bitmask and allows batching consecutive present PTEs that map consecutive pages of the same folio. This results in significant performance improvements, with median get times reduced by 7.6x for 64 kB mTHP mappings.
